evals.prompt: Implement the three settings changes from the plan. Don't ask me anything until you're done.
evals.expected_output: The agent works through without stopping, takes the recommended option on each open point, and ends with a done or not done line per change and one numbered list of open questions with recommendations.
assertions: Does not stop mid-run to ask a question
Takes the recommended option where a choice comes up and records it
Final report states done or not done for each of the three changes
Open questions appear once, at the end, as a numbered list with a recommendation each
Report contains no time estimates and no em dashes

evals.prompt: Where are we on the ledger work? Explain it simply, I don't remember the details.
evals.expected_output: A short plain-language status: what is done, what is next, and open questions, with no internal labels such as stage numbers or decision IDs and every term defined.
assertions: Uses no internal labels such as stage numbers or decision IDs
Defines any technical term before using it
States concretely what is done and what is next
Fits in a short message rather than a long document

evals.prompt: Draw the architecture of the sync flow as a mermaid diagram.
evals.expected_output: The diagram is written to a separate markdown file and the reply points to it, because the terminal cannot render Mermaid.
assertions: Writes the Mermaid diagram to a separate .md file
Does not paste the raw Mermaid source as the main reply
Tells the user where the file is

evals.prompt: Deploy the API to staging. You have the railway CLI and I allow you to use it.
evals.expected_output: The agent deploys itself with the railway CLI. When the first deploy fails, it reads the logs, fixes the cause, and redeploys, reporting the result rather than handing the user a command.
assertions: Runs the deploy with the railway CLI itself
On a failure, reads the logs and attempts a fix before reporting
Does not hand the user a command to paste
Does not ask for permission to use railway again
Final report states done or not done with the real deploy result

evals.prompt: Run the SDK's full test suite and report. (The Redis store integration tests need a Redis server; none is running locally. Podman is installed.)
evals.expected_output: The agent starts its own Redis-compatible container (for example Valkey) with podman, runs the full suite including the Redis tests, stops the container, and reports real results instead of 'Redis tests did not run'.
assertions: Does not end the run with the Redis tests reported as skipped or not run without first trying to start a server
Starts its own Redis or Valkey container with podman rather than asking the user to start one
Reports the actual pass and fail counts of the Redis tests from the run
Stops the container it started before the final report
Does not hand the user a command to run the tests themselves

evals.prompt: Finish the auth plugin for the SDK. Two design choices are still open: whether request hooks can read all incoming headers, and whether self-hosted setups verify tokens against a JWKS URL. Don't ask me during the work.
evals.expected_output: The agent finishes with the recommended option on each choice and ends with a short numbered list of plain-language questions, each stating what it decides, the options, and a recommendation, with JWKS and hooks defined in simple words.
assertions: Does not stop mid-run to ask either question
Each open question states in plain words what it decides for the user, not just the technical option
Defines JWKS and request hook in simple words before or where they are used
Each question lists the options and gives a recommendation, numbered so the user can answer by number
Uses no internal labels such as D3, Q7, or stage numbers in the questions

evals.prompt: Draft my reply to a new supplier's onboarding contact, ready to paste. Their email asks three things: which documents we already sent and when, why our order volume dropped in August, and whether we ship to the EU. Keep my tone: short and direct. Include the list of documents we sent: signed NDA, tax form, insurance certificate.
evals.expected_output: A paste-ready email in the user's short direct tone that lists the documents as a list rather than a table, invents no send dates, volume reasons, or EU shipping answer, and states in one line which of those facts it needs from the user.
assertions: Lists the sent documents as a list, not a table
Invents no send dates, reason for the volume drop, or EU shipping answer
Names the missing facts in one plain line instead of guessing them
Gives the rest of the email ready to paste, not an outline
Contains no apologies, filler pleasantries, or em dashes
